ns2:section.sectionText: This course utilizes literature and history texts, legal documents, and films, both drama and comedy to examine American Indian tribes and indigenous communities throughout the United States. During the semester students will be reading and writing on novels and poems by American Indian authors as well as history and legal texts as a way of understanding and interrogating the politics of race, gender, and cultural genocide as it applies to American Indians. Major themes are øland tenure and clocks,ø øborders and captivity,ø øidentity chosen versus identity imposed,ø øethnic cleansing 101,ø and øreservations and tribal sovereignty.ø This course is writing and reading intensive, highly interactive -- meaning it is driven by student inquiry.
